answers.assumption_check: Assumes handing sys.stdin/stdout/stderr to the child's std handles is enough to reach the caller's output from a no-console parent with an inherited pipe: measured 2026-11-20, 'hi-explicit' printed. Assumes a true console parent also works; unmeasured (needs a visible window), a hypothesis the proof covers where it can. Assumes the tester's OR-merge is the only caller that iterates the returned dict; grep over cairn, bin and skills found it alone.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder would ask: the exact signature (windowless_kwargs(os_name=None, *, given=None)); what given holds (the std keys the caller passes: 'stdin','stdout','stderr'); when to add a stream (not in given and it has a usable fileno, else skip); what to add (sys.stdin/stdout/stderr themselves); how the proof reads a window and output (a no-console parent child via pythonw with a log, nt only, recorded not-run elsewhere). The ticket's decisions carry all of it, and the existing proofs in cairn/tools/windowless_spawn/proofs are the model.

answers.falsifier_check: Falsifier: clause 1, from a no-console pipe parent a bare subprocess.call with **windowless_kwargs(given=()) prints the child's output to the caller; clause 2, from a pythonw parent the same call opens no window and exits 0; clause 3, a caller's own stdout=PIPE still captures and stdout is not duplicated; clause 4, a caller's own stdin is not overwritten; clause 5, windowless_kwargs('nt') with given omitted still returns creationflags only. Horizon: until Windows changes how a CREATE_NO_WINDOW child gets its std handles.
